name: Jon Durbin
title: The midterm results, regardless of your opinion on them, come with a fairly high degree of uncertainly around the future of new datacenter capacity (and/or costs) in the US. Parallax is no longer really optional IMO (though it was already inevitable). “You never change anything by fighting it; you change things by making them obsolete through superior technology.” - R. Buckminster Fuller Status updates: Almost done with dataset prep. It turns out ~10t tokens of high quality data tokenized and properly upsampled and so on is a lot of work and compute. Apple M5 and DGX spark support locked in, still waiting on my AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ PRO 495 from lucebox to get that supported as well. Still chugging away at the final touches on the code/agentic pipeline also (but that would be after the pretraining anyways, non-blocking). Settled on the openai o200k tokenizer, updated to always use single tokens for digits for better math capabilities (hopefully). (and more to come soon)

title: I accidentally forgot to pay the power bill and they turned it off. Happy little accident, because now I get to enjoy the wood stove while re-seating a few hundred 223 rounds (I loaded these originally for a precision bolt action which I traded a few years ago for a 556 and need shorter overall length rounds). Pure zen, memories of hunting trips past, deer season in a couple weeks, good day to zero in the scope too.

title: NVIDIA's GR00T 2 is learning robot skills from human video and transferring them to machines that never performed the task before. After five demonstrations per task and a 30-minute fine-tune on one RTX 5090, the model reached 95% average success across 50 tasks. It can also work with a reasoning agent that sequences tasks, checks progress, and calls recovery skills. Full details ↓ https://www.tao.media/nvidia-unveils-gr00t-2-to-transfer-human-skills-to-robots/
